title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals
claim: Our method preserves fine detail and achieves the best quality with far fewer faces than competing methods.
layout: 2 stacked rows: zoomed baseline crops on top; scatter plot plus renderings below
description: The figure has two rows split by a dashed line. The top row shows a bookshelf scene on the left, with red boxes marking two regions. To its right is a 2x2 grid of zoomed crops from Ours, 2DGS, MeshSplatting and MiLo. Each crop shows text on book spines and on an 'ALGORITHMS' book, with PSNR and LPIPS values in a caption bar. Ours is sharp and has its values highlighted in yellow. The baselines are blurry or distorted. The bottom row has a scatter plot of PSNR (dB) against number of faces (millions) with a broken x-axis. A red star marks Ours at the top left, which is high PSNR with few faces. MeshSplatting, MiLo, 2DGS, RaDe-GS and GOF sit lower or further right. To the right are three panels of a garden table scene: Rendering, Normal map and Mesh.
caption: Top: our method better preserves high-frequency details (e.g., text) than MeshSplatting [ref] and MiLo [ref] on the shelf scene (STRinGS-360 [ref]). Bottom: on the garden scene, T$^2$-Splat achieves the highest PSNR (25.68\,dB) among the compared methods using only 2.7M faces, versus 92M for GOF [ref] and 15M for MiLo [ref].
abstract: Triangle-based splatting connects novel view synthesis with conventional graphics pipelines, but often requires excessive tessellation to preserve appearance details. We present T$^2$-Splat, which decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement. Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation (Safe RDT) initializes mesh connectivity. Dynamic Topology Evolution (DTE) then adapts triangle allocation through edge collapse and vertex split operations. Residual per-face Mip-textures then refine appearance on the fixed mesh using scale-adaptive filtering. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and DTU demonstrate competitive results with compact meshes. T$^2$-Splat improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360. Additional compression experiments demonstrate flexible control of mesh complexity, supporting face budgets as low as 10% of the original face count. Project page: https://t2-splat.github.io/.
